content: L-lysine, also known as lysine monohydrochloride, is prescribed with specific dosing regimens depending on the indication. For oral administration, a dose of 1000 mg is typically taken once to three times daily (qD-TID) for a duration of 6 to 12 months. For topical application, a product such as Super Lysine Plus is applied every two hours (q2hr) for 11 days. In cases requiring higher doses, 10 grams per day may be divided into multiple doses and administered orally for up to 5 days. L-lysine is used for various purposes, including enhancing athletic performance, managing herpes simplex labialis, and treating metabolic alkalosis. It is considered possibly effective for the treatment of herpes simplex labialis. Reported adverse effects include diarrhea, abdominal pain, chronic renal failure, and interstitial nephritis. However, no significant drug interactions have been reported. L-lysine is contraindicated in individuals with kidney disease. Regarding pregnancy and lactation, the use of L-lysine is generally advised against. It is categorized as Pregnancy Category A, meaning that controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. However, its use during pregnancy and lactation is still recommended to be avoided. Cost information for L-lysine may vary depending on the formulation and dosage.
